title: After you submit
intro: This page only restates what the official documents in our package say about what follows a submission. Where they are silent we say so. It tracks process; it says nothing about whether any application will be accepted.
unknown_text: Not published in the materials we have - ask your authority.

common.text: A written variance may be issued by an Administrator or a safety codes officer, who must be of the opinion that it provides approximately equivalent or greater safety performance. The decision is theirs, not this tool's.
The Safety Codes Council itself can also issue a variance, for example when it hears an appeal of a refusal.
On the official form, Part 2 is completed by the Safety Codes Officer responsible for reviewing the variance, who either issues the variance (Part 2a) or refuses it (Part 2b).

scc.text: The whole form, with all supporting documentation, is forwarded to the Safety Codes Council, Administrator of Accreditation (accreditation@safetycodes.ab.ca).

calgary.text: Variances are requested by the owner or the owner's agent to a safety codes officer in the building discipline. A variance may only be issued by an SCO, a technical administrator, or the Safety Codes Council.

Your application and documents are reviewed by the applicable parties within Inspections & Permit Services, and the SCO may ask for further representation, for example that the Architect also take part.

edmonton.text: For Point Access Block proposals, the pre-application meeting is with a Development Planner and Safety Codes officers, including Building Permit reviewers.

edmonton: Which Edmonton office issues the variance after you submit, and how you send it: no Edmonton-specific variance procedure was found in the materials.

common.text: Part 2(a): a variance is issued, and the officer may set conditions that must be met.

Part 2(b): the variance is refused. The form lists three reasons the officer ticks: the Part 1 information is incorrect; it is not sufficient or complete enough for the officer to decide; or the officer is not satisfied the alternative gives approximately equivalent or greater safety performance. The officer may add written rationale.
A refusal is served on the applicant in writing; the form records the date and the format in which it was served.
Once a variance is issued, the owner or other responsible person must ensure its terms and conditions are complied with.

calgary.text: A request may be accepted, refused, or you may be asked for further information. If accepted, the SCO issues a formal variance that includes any conditions.
A variance request can only be accepted if a building permit has been applied for; a variance number cannot be issued without a building permit number.

all: What format an officer's questions arrive in, and how many rounds of questions are normal: the SCC form does not describe a request-for-information step. Only the Calgary guide says you may be asked for further information.

sections.title: If a variance is refused: appeal

common.text: An applicant who receives a written refusal may appeal it to the Safety Codes Council in line with the Council's bylaws, within 30 days. The Act counts from the date the notice is received; the form counts from the date the refusal was served. Check the date on your notice.
The form states: all appeals must be made within 30 days of the date the Refusal was served.

An appeal request must be in writing on the Council's Notice of Appeal and signed by the appellant; include a copy of Part 1 and Part 2(b); concisely state the grounds; give the appellant's name, address, telephone and email; and be accompanied by the fee in the Council fee schedule.
Send it to the Safety Codes Council, Coordinator of Appeals, 500, 1405 Jasper Avenue NW, Edmonton AB T5J 3N4; appeals@safetycodes.ab.ca; 780-413-0099 (toll free 1-888-413-0099).
The appeal process is not available to applications that were reviewed and refused by an Administrator of the Safety Codes Act; an Administrator's decision on a variance is final.
On an appeal the Council may confirm the refusal, or revoke it and issue a written variance on terms it considers appropriate.

calgary.text: Calgary's guide states the appeal needs a Notice of Appeal Form, a copy of the Written Notice, and the $500 appeal fee, within 30 days from the date of service of the Written Notice of Variance Refusal. It applies to refusals issued since December 1, 2021.

scc: The appeal fee amount: the form refers to the Council fee schedule, which is not in the materials. The $500 figure is stated only in Calgary's guide.
edmonton: The appeal fee amount: the form refers to the Council fee schedule, which is not in the materials. The $500 figure is stated only in Calgary's guide.
all: How long the Council takes to decide an appeal.

common.text: General guidance (not an Alberta authority's commitment): allow one to two months for correspondence, depending on complexity. Few or no jurisdictions publish approval timelines, since approval depends on the submission.
General guidance: some jurisdictions give feedback within a month, but that is a documentation check, not a full review; it is good practice to allow two to four months to receive comments.

all: How long your authority takes to review a variance and respond: no authority-specific review timeline is published in the materials.
Any fee for submitting a variance request: none is stated in the form or the guides.

common.text: By signing, you accept that the information is shared with the Safety Codes Council, and that some non-personal information from the form may be published on the Council website.
An Administrator may place an entry on the information system briefly indicating the subject of a variance and the location it applies to (a variance register).

calgary.text: Variances are site specific: a variance covering more than one permit or building needs a separate request for each permit or site, and a separate form for each different issue.
